skill.name: broken-authentication
skill.description: Guides authorized security testers through broken authentication and session management assessment for web applications.
skill.summary: Assess password, session, MFA, and password reset controls for authorized web application security testing.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most external-command detections are Markdown fence false positives, not executable backtick usage. The skill still contains high-risk authentication attack workflows, including brute-force testing, credential-stuffing evasion, MFA bypass, session fixation, JWT forgery, and password-reset account takeover techniques. Publication should require stronger authorization gating and removal or narrowing of offensive execution guidance.

remediation.issue: Credential attack procedures include brute-force commands, breached credential workflows, and evasion tactics.
remediation.suggestion: Replace executable attack steps with defensive validation checklists, safe lab examples, and rate-limit verification guidance.

remediation.issue: MFA, session fixation, JWT forgery, and password reset sections provide operational account takeover workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Reframe these sections as control checks with expected secure behavior and remove step-by-step exploit replay instructions.

remediation.issue: Network testing guidance can be applied to real systems without an explicit runtime authorization gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear confirmation of written authorization, target scope, and test accounts before any network-facing testing steps.

remediation.issue: Examples use public-looking domains and realistic account identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Use reserved documentation domains, local lab targets, and non-sensitive placeholder identities throughout the examples.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Attack and Evasion Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill provides brute-force and credential-stuffing procedures, including Hydra usage, breached credential pairs, and source IP or user-agent rotation guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections explicitly cover brute force testing, credential stuffing, credential payloads, and lockout bypass via IP rotation. Authorization language exists, but the procedures are directly usable for account attack workflows.

semantic_findings.title: MFA Bypass Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs OTP brute forcing, direct URL MFA skipping, response manipulation, empty OTP submission, OTP reuse, and API version downgrade testing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The MFA section lists multiple concrete bypass methods and payload strategies. These are legitimate in a lab, but harmful if applied outside authorized scope.

semantic_findings.title: Account Takeover Through Session and Reset Abuse
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes session fixation and password reset token manipulation workflows that can transfer or reset another user account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections describe fixed-session victim login and changing reset user parameters. These are clear account takeover paths when controls are vulnerable.

semantic_findings.title: JWT Token Forgery Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill walks through modifying a JWT to use the none algorithm, changing the role to admin, and submitting the modified bearer token.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example gives a complete token forgery flow with role escalation and replay. It is clearly a security test, but it is operationally useful for unauthorized privilege escalation.

content.value_statement: Authentication flaws can lead to account takeover and data exposure. This skill guides authorized testers through structured checks for passwords, sessions, MFA, and reset flows.
actual_capabilities: Maps authentication endpoints and login workflows.
Reviews password policy and account lockout behavior.
Tests username enumeration and rate-limit controls.
Evaluates session token handling, fixation, and timeout controls.
Assesses MFA enrollment, OTP handling, and recovery workflows.
Reviews password reset token security and account binding.
limitations: Requires written authorization and scoped test accounts.
Does not verify that a target is safe or legally approved.
Some tests can disrupt accounts or trigger monitoring controls.
Results depend on target configuration and available permissions.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Authentication Test Plan
use_cases.description: Define scoped checks for login, lockout, password policy, and enumeration before a web application assessment.

use_cases.title: Review Session Management
use_cases.description: Assess cookie flags, session regeneration, timeout behavior, and logout handling for an application release.

use_cases.title: Validate Remediation
use_cases.description: Retest authentication fixes and document whether previous findings are resolved with clear evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Scoped Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized broken authentication test plan for [application]. Scope is [environment], test accounts are [accounts], and excluded areas are [limits].

prompt_templates.title: Assess Session Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the session management controls for [application]. Focus on cookie flags, token regeneration, idle timeout, absolute timeout, and logout invalidation.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate MFA and Reset Flows
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess MFA and password reset security for [application]. Use only authorized test accounts and summarize risks, evidence needed, and safe remediation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an Executive Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these authentication test notes into a concise report with scope, findings, severity, business impact, evidence summary, and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Review login, reset, and MFA flows for a scoped staging application.
output_examples.output: A structured assessment plan covering test accounts, allowed endpoints, control checks, evidence needs, and safe stopping conditions.

output_examples.input: Summarize session management findings from tester notes.
output_examples.output: A finding summary with affected controls, risk rating, observed behavior, user impact, and remediation recommendations.

output_examples.input: Prepare a retest checklist for authentication fixes.
output_examples.output: A focused checklist for lockout, enumeration, MFA recovery, session timeout, reset token binding, and reporting evidence.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, and test accounts before any assessment.
Prefer staging or lab environments when testing disruptive authentication behavior.
Record evidence carefully and stop testing when controls show unsafe behavior.
anti_patterns: Testing production users or real breached credentials without explicit approval.
Running brute-force or bypass tests before defining limits and monitoring contacts.
Reporting exploit steps without clear remediation and business impact.

faq.question: What does this skill assess?
faq.answer: It assesses password policy, account lockout, enumeration, sessions, MFA, and password reset controls.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Use it only for authorized security testing by trained testers, application security teams, or approved auditors.

faq.question: Can it test production systems?
faq.answer: Production testing requires explicit written approval, defined rate limits, test accounts, and monitoring coordination.

faq.question: Does it replace a full penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports authentication review, but broader application logic, infrastructure, and monitoring still need separate assessment.

faq.question: What evidence should testers collect?
faq.answer: Collect scoped request details, timestamps, affected controls, observed behavior, screenshots when appropriate, and remediation validation notes.

faq.question: How should risky tests be handled?
faq.answer: Run risky tests in staging when possible, use test accounts, set stop conditions, and coordinate with system owners.
